authors_reviews.title: Windproof plasma arc and brilliant LED power display—the ultimate elegant, mess-free lighter!
authors_reviews.text: I am highly satisfied with the innovative design and absolute reliability of this FUKKUDA electric candle lighter. Powered by advanced flameless plasma arc technology, it completely eliminates the hassle of smelly fluid refills or burning your fingertips, igniting deeply recessed candle wicks and indoor fireplaces instantly. The windproof and splashproof design works flawlessly under any weather conditions, while the real-time LED battery indicator removes all power anxiety by letting you track your charge status at a glance. It packs an exceptional layer of safety with a dual-action child-lock switch and a smart 7-second automatic shutoff mechanism to ensure absolute peace of mind when stored in a drawer. The ultra-slim aluminum alloy frame and elegant rose gold finish look beautiful on any countertop—making it a perfect everyday asset for setting a cozy home ambiance!
authors_reviews.author: Kultawat Chandarkaew

authors_reviews.title: Sleek, Modern, and Reliable—A Huge Upgrade from Traditional Lighters
authors_reviews.text: I recently purchased this Electric Candle Lighter, and overall, I’m giving it a solid 4/5 stars. After using traditional butane lighters for years, making the switch to this flameless, USB-rechargeable option has been a total game-changer for my candle-lighting routine.The design is incredibly sleek. It feels premium in the hand with a satisfying weight—not too heavy, but sturdy enough that it doesn’t feel like cheap plastic. The long, flexible neck is perfect for reaching deep into jar candles without burning my fingers or tilting the container and risking wax spills. It’s also completely windproof, which makes it far more reliable than a standard flick-lighter when I’m lighting candles in drafty rooms.The safety switch design is intuitive and well-placed, giving me peace of mind that it won’t accidentally trigger in a drawer. It’s very easy to use, and the USB charging feature is convenient, eliminating the need to constantly buy replacements.However, I am knocking off one star because the battery life is slightly shorter than I anticipated. It seems to discharge relatively quickly, which means I have to keep it plugged in more often than I’d like. While it charges fast, it would be nice to have a larger capacity battery for longer-term use.Despite the frequent charging, the value for money is excellent. It looks elegant sitting on my coffee table, feels comfortable to hold, and functions exactly as advertised. If you’re tired of butane lighters failing you, this is a fantastic, eco-friendly upgrade that I would definitely recommend to any fellow candle enthusiast.
authors_reviews.author: madnuk

authors_reviews.title: No-compromise upgrade over a traditional lighter
authors_reviews.text: I've had one of these for a few months now at least. As mentioned in the review title, it's literally just a straight upgrade to a traditional lighter with no downsides I can see so far. One key feature this unit has that others like it don't is the dual-arc feature. Most arc lighters (in 2023) are single-arc - these work fine but you have less surface area AKA you have to be more precise and it might take a little longer to get flames going. The dual arc feature effectively gives you a "plane" of plasma to push into what ever you're lighting instead of a single line - easier, faster, and really bridges the gap between arc and traditional lighters (pun intended).To compare with traditional lighters, let's imagine we're using one of the traditional long-neck versions. You hold the tip to your candle and pull the trigger. Nothing happens (because there was no gas when you pulled the trigger). You pull it again and the flame lights. Now, you may not think much of this, because this is just the normal experience of a lighter, but it will stick out like a sore thumb after using an arc lighter: when you pull the trigger on an arc lighter, you get an arc. Every time. Wind, rain, sleet, or snow.Let's say you were maybe not so prepared and somehow allowed your lighter to get low and run out of fuel. I think many of us have a backup lighter (or ten) somewhere since they're so cheap. I'd still recommend doing that, but I don't expect to use mine. I'm not sure about you but I have much more convenient access to electricity than I do to lighter fluid. Since the arc lighter is an electric device, it can report how much battery it has left very easily (this one uses 4 LEDs corresponding to 25% increments). When you see the LEDs getting low, you just plug it in (just like you would your phone). I've had to charge mine twice, but even if I had to do it 200 times by now - it's so easy to do, and so easy to know that you need to do it, that it does not matter.And... that's really it. Is it going to change your life? No. But it's a useful tool and it's superior to traditional lighters. I like that it allows me to not need to use fuel, both for monetary reasons and for the admittedly infinitesimally small positive impact to taking care of our planet. I don't see any reason to not have one as my primary lighter ever in the future, and right now, this specific model is the one I recommend, until a triple arc model comes out, or one that is more obviously user serviceable in the event of device failures (this one may be, but I can't confirm)
